title: Wrap a local function
summary: LangChain is a collection of tools for connecting application steps. RunnableLambda wraps a Python function so it can use a common interface.
introduction: LangChain is a collection of tools for connecting application steps. RunnableLambda wraps a Python function so it can use a common interface. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: LangChain is a collection of tools for connecting application steps. RunnableLambda wraps a Python function so it can use a common interface.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These Python examples need the langchain-core package in a separate environment. Every function here is local. Prompt text is prepared but never sent to a model by this tutorial.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of LangChain. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
clean = RunnableLambda(lambda text: text.strip())
print(clean.invoke("  Moon  "))
blocks.title: Wrap a local function

blocks.text: The output is Moon without outside spaces. strip removes those spaces, and invoke runs the wrapped function once. No language model is involved.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try input with spaces only and inspect the empty string.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A runnable is a step in a program, not automatically an AI model.
For more detail later, use this [LangChain further reading](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/overview).
